anomalies.observed: In the POWER TRAIN block, two TVS diodes sit in parallel from the +24V input node (after F2) to GND: D1 is marked 28V and D2 is marked 12V. A 12 V TVS across a 24 V rail is in continuous breakdown.
anomalies.expected: The specification calls for a single 28 V TVS (D2 — SMBJ28A, '24 V-rail clamp') on the 24 V input. A clamp on the 24 V rail must have a standoff voltage above 24 V (e.g. SMBJ28A), not 12 V.

evidence.quote: POWER TRAIN (sheet 1): F2 7A -> +24V node with D1 28V and D2 12V both tied from +24V to GND
D2 — SMBJ28A TVS | Input surge/overvoltage protection on the 24 V rail | ... ('28V,' DO-214AA TVS) matches a 24 V-rail clamp

anomalies.impact: The 12 V TVS will conduct as soon as the 24 V supply rises above ~12–13 V, clamping the input rail well below its nominal 24 V, dissipating large current and almost certainly blowing the 7 A input fuse (F2). The board would fail to power up / the buck and 24 V loads would not receive 24 V.

parsed.summary: The schematic shows a 12 V TVS (D2) placed in parallel with the 28 V TVS (D1) directly across the +24 V input rail, contradicting the specified 28 V SMBJ28A clamp; a 12 V clamp on a 24 V rail would conduct continuously and blow the input fuse, preventing the board from powering up. Other apparent differences (LiDAR on I2C, reference-number shifts, firmware GPIO mismatches) correspond to documented design choices/known limitations and are not reported as anomalies.
